LESSON: LETTER SOUND CORRESPONDENCE.

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: READING
Topic 2.2: Letter Sound correspondence.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Letter Sound correspondence., part of READING in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we learn about letter sounds? 2. Which letters of the alphabet do we like most? Why?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. Identify letters of the alphabet by name,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Letter Sound correspondence. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. Identify letter sounds from a variety of texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Letter Sound correspondence. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. Match letter names and letter sounds appropriately,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Letter Sound correspondence. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. participate in chanting rhymes on letter names and letter sounds. ● Watch an animated clip on letters and letter sounds, identify letters of the alphabet and read the sounds from a chart. Adjust light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light. ● Identify letters from books, charts, flash cards, digital devices. ● Read letter sounds in turns from chart, books, boards, flash cards, digital devices. Learners with speech difficulties could read an audiobook or use adapted digital devices with audio visuals with subtitles to read pictures. ● Chant rhymes on letter names and letter sounds in 1. Why do we learn about letter sounds? 2. Which letters of the alphabet do we like most? Why? 45 turns and collaboratively in the right order, (Letter a, sound /a /, Letter b, sound /b/......). Learners with speech difficulties could point at the sounds as they are read to them.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Letter Sound correspondence. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
